newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss delay decision on gene-altered soy imports.
newsitem.headline: Swiss delay decision on gene-altered soy imports.

text.p: The Swiss Federal Department of the Interior (EDI) said it decided Friday to delay imports of gene-altered soy as it considered complaints from private citizens and some organisations.
Earlier in December the Swiss Federal Health Agency (BAG) said it had allowed U.S. agricultural, chemcials and pharmaceuticals group Monsanto Co to import the soy.
Permission for the imports was supposed to be granted February 1, but delayed by complaints.

"The Federal Department of the Interior confirmed that the complaints about introduction of gene-technically altered soy in foodstuffs would have a delaying impact" on imports, the EDI said in a statement issued Friday.
"Until a final decision is reached, which is likely to be in March 1997, no foodstuffs containing gene-technically altered soy will be imported into Switzerland and sold on the market," the EDI said.
A spokesman for the EDI, elaborating on the statement, said that the decision may be expected by mid-March.
Monsanto also has the option of contesting the decision in Switzerland's supreme court in Lausanne.
No-one at Monsanto's offices was immediately available for comment.

Swiss private individuals and Swiss health food stores were among those opposing import of gene-altered soy. The worldwide environmental organisation Greenpeace also supported measures opposing its import.
